name: Perturbation Theory
description: Systematic computation method for perturbative expansions in QFT and related fields

steps.action: Identify the expansion parameter (coupling α, λ, g) and verify it is small enough for perturbation theory to be valid
steps.checkpoint: Is α < 1? Is the expansion parameter the correct physical coupling?

steps.action: Determine the order of expansion needed (tree-level, one-loop, two-loop) based on the claim and accuracy requirements
steps.checkpoint: Does the claim specify the required order? Does the deliverable match this order?

steps.action: Draw Feynman diagrams for all diagrams at the desired order using the correct Feynman rules for the chosen gauge and conventions
steps.checkpoint: All diagrams accounted for? No missing topology? Correct vertex factors for gauge choice?

steps.action: Write the amplitude for each diagram, tracking momentum flow, vertex factors, and propagators consistent with convention lock
steps.checkpoint: ASSERT_CONVENTION line present? Metric signature consistent? Propagator form matches gauge choice?

steps.action: Regularize divergences (dimensional regularization, cutoff, Pauli-Villars) consistent with the chosen renormalization scheme
steps.checkpoint: Regularization matches renormalization_scheme from lock? ε poles correctly tracked?

steps.action: Apply renormalization conditions (on-shell, MS-bar, MOM) to define counterterms and subtract divergences
steps.checkpoint: Counterterm definitions match renormalization_scheme? No double-counting of subtractions?

steps.action: Compute the finite remainder at the desired order and verify it matches the claimed result
steps.checkpoint: Use spot_check.py for numerical verification. Compare against literature benchmarks.

red_flags: Expansion parameter α > 1 — perturbation theory not valid
Missing diagrams at given order (e.g., forgetting crossed channels)
Using tree-level Feynman rules for loop diagrams
Gauge parameter ξ appearing in physical observables
UV divergence treated inconsistently (mixing regularization schemes)
IR divergence not handled (massless particles, soft limits)
Counterterm subtraction at wrong order (over/under subtraction)
Mixing renormalization schemes within same calculation
Wrong spin sum / polarization sum (using wrong convention for ε^μ)
common_errors: E02: Metric signature flip in propagator
